spans.context: What Is School Choice?  School choice is a term that represents the many ways students access their K–12 education.  Many still choose their schools by buying a home in their desired district, but today’s parents engage in school choice in more diverse and ever-evolving ways.

spans.text: A new report from the Government Accountability Office mirrors data on the closure rates of federally funded charter schools that the Biden administration cited in its controversial push for more oversight when it comes to charter school funding.
spans.context:
RECOVERED SOURCE TEXT
 A new report from the Government Accountability Office mirrors data on the closure rates of federally funded charter schools that the Biden administration cited in its controversial push for more oversight when it comes to charter school funding.
 But it also finds that, overall, charters that received federal money were less likely to close within five years than those that did not.

spans.text: Charter school proponents assert that charter schools are not given the opportunities to restructure often and are simply closed down when students perform poorly on these assessments.[21]
spans.context: Typically, these schools are allowed to remain open, perhaps with new leadership or restructuring, or perhaps with no change at all.  Charter school proponents assert that charter schools are not given the opportunities to restructure often and are simply closed down when students perform poorly on these assessments.[21]  As of March 2009[update], 12.5% of the over 5000 charter schools founded in the United States had closed for reasons including academic, financial, and managerial problems, and occasionally consolidation or district interference.[22]

spans.text: Moreover, the authors conclude: "charter schools with a strong academic focus and "no-excuses" philosophy that serve poor black students in urban areas stand as contradictions to the general association between school-level poverty and academic achievement. These very high-poverty, high-minority schools produce achievement gains that are substantially greater than the traditional public schools in the same catchment areas."[134] This study concludes that "charter schools are also, on average, more racially segregated than traditional public schools," and state "reducing school segregation and improving the quality of schools serving minority students are both important goals, but they are not the same".[134]
spans.context:
However, a recent statistical analysis of racial segregation and performance outcomes in U.S. charter schools notes that studies on race and charter schools often incorrectly confound the inter-dependent variables of race and family income (poverty).[133]  Moreover, the authors conclude: "charter schools with a strong academic focus and "no-excuses" philosophy that serve poor black students in urban areas stand as contradictions to the general association between school-level poverty and academic achievement. These very high-poverty, high-minority schools produce achievement gains that are substantially greater than the traditional public schools in the same catchment areas."[134] This study concludes that "charter schools are also, on average, more racially segregated than traditional public schools," and state "reducing school segregation and improving the quality of schools serving minority students are both important goals, but they are not the same".[134]

spans.context: Charter school proponents assert that charter schools are not given the opportunities to restructure often and are simply closed down when students perform poorly on these assessments.[21]  As of March 2009[update], 12.5% of the over 5000 charter schools founded in the United States had closed for reasons including academic, financial, and managerial problems, and occasionally consolidation or district interference.[22]  A 2013 Study by the Center for Research on Education Outcomes (CREDO) at Stanford University institute linked overall improvement of the charter school sector to charter school closures, suggesting that charter schools as a whole are not getting better, but the closure of bad schools is improving the system as a whole.[23]

claimPosition.reason: Evidence shows Biden supports charter schools and does not advocate for their closure. Additionally, studies suggest charter schools can improve outcomes for minority students, contradicting the claim that closing them would benefit Black and Hispanic children.
